The last lap saw the leaders racing in real earnest, Tebbutt (S.L.H.) going away with Bert in close attendance until Bert made his big effort and went away to win a glorious race in 46 mins. 9 secs., about 80—100 yds. ahead of the second man.

Carter being up in the front, with Weatherill and Tebbutt of S.L.H. At the first lap Weatherill was "out on his own" and, politely inquiring how far he was in front, seemed to draw further ahead; but it was very gratifying to see a "Claret and Gold" in second place, carried by Carter, with Tebbutt at his shoulder.
Shepherd, 7 min. 28 secs. 4 x 110 yards relay; 2nd., Bels. (Rae, Picton, Tebbutt, Marshall).

In the Junior 4 x 110 yards relay our team comprising: Marshall, Tebbutt, Rae and Sexton, in that order, won their heat in 45,5 secs. In the final they drew lane 4, on the outside, and thanks to an almost super human effort by Alan Sexton, after bad baton handling earlier, won in 45.3 secs.

Sexton won his first heat in 24.1; Tebbutt won his first heat in 24.6; Picton, Marshall and Rae were each second in their heats. Sexton beat Marshall in the second round in 23.6; Picton won his second round in 23.9.
